title: Architecture description
description: Compact, durable description of a software system for orientation of agents and humans and for guarding architecture against drift. List items start with a key naming their type and holding the id (component: payments); endpoints and external systems are maps keyed by id. Ids are unique per scope: top-level items share one namespace, items nested in a component share another. Entity names are unique system-wide. Relations (uses, calls, produces, consumes, reads, writes) are an allowlist: a module may do what its component declares plus what the module itself declares; anything else is a violation. Arrow items (flows, states) are 'a -> b' or 'a -> b: label'; quote them when the label contains ': '. Objects are open: add fields as needed. Value sets are listed in descriptions and checked by the check utility.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what the system is and its main shape.

decisions.description: Path to ADRs. Link, never retell.

tech.description: System-wide overview, not inherited. Keys: languages, deploy, ci, e2e, observability, ... Values: string or list.

glossary.description: Domain terms. Value: optional note when the meaning is non-obvious.

actors.description: People and agents using the system, keyed by id. Keys: does (required), uses (components they work with directly; each component's ui_endpoints say how).

external.description: Third-party systems, keyed by id. Keys: does (required), protocol, address, calls (our endpoints it calls inbound, e.g. [payments.stripe-webhooks]).

items.description: Relations declared on a component apply to all its modules; a module adds its own on top.

type.description: service (serves requests) | worker (triggered by consumed events or its own schedule endpoint) | web-app | mobile-app | desktop-app | console-app (CLI run by a person).

source_path.description: Code directory relative to repo root, e.g. 'core/'.

endpoints.description: API surfaces or channels (not single operations) that services and clients consume, keyed by id. Synchronous APIs and triggers; messaging goes to root queues. A schedule endpoint is the component's own trigger (address: cron). Protocols: http, grpc, graphql, websocket, schedule, file, ... for: component or external ids, or a short name for consumers outside the model, e.g. partner-apps.

ui_endpoints.description: Entry points for people and agents, keyed by id; same structure as endpoints, and not targets of calls. Protocols: http (web UI), cli, native (mobile or desktop), mcp, ... for: actor ids.

datastores.description: Private to this component, access implicit.

modules.description: Root modules: shared libraries, not separately deployable.

datastores.description: Root datastores: shared, every access declared with reads/writes.

queues.description: Topics and queues: shared, every use declared with produces/consumes. Keys: queue (required), engine (kafka 3, rabbitmq, ...), deploy (sqs, pubsub, confluent-cloud, ...), address (topic/queue name), schema_owner (component owning the message contract), entities (message types).

states.description: Lifecycles where an illegal transition costs money or trust. Keyed by '<entity>.<field>' (or '<entity>' when the field is obvious). Items: 'from -> to' with an optional trigger label. Any transition not listed is illegal.

flows.description: One to three main success paths, keyed by name. Steps in order. Participants: actor, external, component, '<component>.<module>', datastore, queue. 'a -> b: label' is a sync call, allowed by a's calls (b, b's component or one of its endpoints), an actor's uses, reads/writes for a datastore, or uses between two modules of one component. 'a ~> b: message' is async; message is an entity of a queue that a produces and b consumes.

rules.description: Only rules that relations can't express.

level.description: must: a violation blocks the merge (failing check, or reviewer when no check). should: a violation is allowed with a stated reason in the change; a check only warns.

applies_to.description: Selector; omitted = whole system. Keys (AND): components, modules, queues, type, language, protocol, relation (uses, calls, produces, consumes, reads, writes), paths. Values: lists (OR).

check.description: Path to the automated check. Omitted = enforced by review.

endpoint.description: Keys: protocol (required), for and auth (required except on schedule endpoints), address, spec, summary, idempotent (true: safe to retry).

for.description: Target audience: who is expected to consume this endpoint.

auth.description: 'none' for an open endpoint, or auth protocol (oauth2, oidc, saml, api-key, mtls, webhook-signature, ...) -> identity providers or issuers, e.g. {oauth2: [google, apple, keycloak]}.

tech.description: Notable items as 'name major-version'. Keys: language, build, runtime, frameworks, messaging, test, observability, deploy (where it runs: gke, cloud-run, cloud-sql, ...), ... Values: string or list.

access.description: Store or queue id -> entity names (null = not detailed).

arrow.description: 'a -> b' or 'a -> b: label' (sync, or a state transition); 'a ~> b: label' (async).

relations.description: Outbound relations. Own endpoints and nested datastores are implicit. A bare id inside a component resolves to its own module first, then to a top-level item.

uses.description: Code dependencies on modules: sibling, root or 'core.catalog'. Compile by default; suffix ' runtime' or ' test'.

calls.description: Synchronous calls: endpoints ('payments.payments-api'), external systems, or a whole component (coarse).

consumes.description: Queue -> message entities consumed. Also a trigger of the component.

module.description: Code unit with a structural or functional role: distinct business value, API or SPI contracts, entity definitions, a lot of code, or many dependencies in or out. Not every package is a module; relations of code outside listed modules go on its component. Nested in a component or at root (shared library). Relations on a nested module are allowed for that module only, in addition to the component's.

serves.description: Endpoints and ui_endpoints of its component that this module handles. Nested modules only; one endpoint can be served by several modules.

datastore.description: Data store. Nested: private, access implicit. Root: shared. Keys: datastore (required), engine (postgresql 16, redis 7, gcs, ...), deploy (cloud-sql, ...), entities (tables, collections, buckets), source_path (migrations), schema_owner (root: owning component).

entities.description: Keyed by entity name. Value: list of fields, or null. Keys and references are the useful minimum; add other fields when where the data lives matters. Field markers: 'pk' primary key (several = composite), 'uk' unique, 'uk1', 'uk2' composite unique groups, '-> entity' reference to its pk, '-> entity.field' to another field (across stores = logical). Combine: 'order_id pk -> orders'.
